# Release watcher: operations guide

Version 1.0.0 of the specification: 1 monitor, 2 jobs, 0 dependencies and 0 endpoints. For the people who run the live system: where it runs, what to look at each day, what to do when a monitor's objective is missed, what runs on its own, what it depends on, and how its data is saved and brought back.

## 1. Where it runs

| Environment | Purpose | Promotes to |
|---|---|---|
| production | The host the watcher runs on. |   |

## 2. Daily checklist

What to look at on the live system each day. Tick the last column as each is seen to be as expected.

| Check | What to look at | Expected | Seen |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monitor watcher-running (production) | Whether the watcher runs. | It runs at every hour of the day. |   |
| Job sweep | Its last run, every PT1M. | It ran, and failed on no item. |   |
| Job prune | Its last run, on the schedule `0 3 * * *` (UTC). | It ran, and failed on no item. |   |
| Process releaseWatcher | That it is running. | It is running and healthy: it has asked the registry within the last two minutes. |   |
| Process pruner | Its last run. | It ran, and exited 0. |   |
| Process diskReport | Its last run. | It ran, and exited 0. |   |

## 3. Monitors

### watcher-running

Whether the watcher runs. In production. Objective: It runs at every hour of the day.

The specification does not say what to do when the objective is missed; the steps are written under the monitor's response.

## 4. Jobs

What the system runs on its own. A job acts as its role and may do only what the role's permissions allow.

| Job | Starts | Acts as | After a failure | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sweep | every PT1M | installer | not tried again | Looks for a new release and installs it. |
| prune | on the schedule `0 3 * * *` (UTC) | installer | not tried again | Removes releases older than the last three. |

## 5. Processes

The programs the service manager starts and watches. A process acts as no role: the jobs it runs act as theirs.

| Process | Runs | Jobs | Restarted | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| releaseWatcher | always, from the host's start | sweep | when it fails, after PT5S; given up after 5 starts within PT10M | Asks the registry for a new release of each service and installs it. |
| pruner | when a job it runs is due | prune | never | Prunes old releases at night. |
| diskReport | every PT6H |   | not said | Writes how much disk the releases take. |

### releaseWatcher

Reads the settings registryAddress, registryToken when it starts; the section Settings says what each is.

| Signal | What it does |
|---|---|
| SIGTERM | finishes the release it is installing, then exits 0, within PT30S |
| SIGHUP | reads its settings again |

| Exit status | Meaning | Started again |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | it was asked to stop | as Restarted says |
| 78 | a setting is wrong | never |

Healthy when it has asked the registry within the last two minutes. Looked at every PT1M.

Watched by the monitor watcher-running; the section Monitors says what to do when one is missed.
